title: Architectural Blueprinting for Distributed Logistics
business: A regional logistics firm managing complex warehouse automation workflows.
problem: Technical leads struggle to maintain alignment on evolving warehouse floor layouts, leading to costly miscommunications during physical infrastructure upgrades.
solution: By utilizing the Excalidraw MCP connector, the team generates real-time, hand-drawn style architectural diagrams directly within Claude. This allows stakeholders to visualize spatial constraints and process flows immediately after discussing requirements, ensuring all parties share a common visual reference.
steps: Initiate the Excalidraw MCP tool within the Claude interface to establish a persistent canvas session.
Describe the warehouse floor constraints and automation node requirements to Claude to generate the initial diagram.
Use the create_view tool to define specific focus areas for different logistics teams.
Save the current state using save_checkpoint to create a versioned history of the layout iterations.
Export the final diagram via export_to_excalidraw for integration into official facility documentation.
outcome: Improved clarity in cross-departmental planning and a significant reduction in design-to-implementation errors.
limitation: The connector relies on the current MCP session state; if the session is cleared or the checkpoint is not saved, previous iterations are lost. Users should verify their progress by checking the saved history periodically.
